## Acceptance criteria

REQ-01 fails: the generated lock-timeout scope inaccurately excludes general `.jit` storage locks from `JIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT`. REQ-02/03 are otherwise addressed.

## Architecture and functional style

No new layer-boundary or functional-style violation found.

## Correctness and safety

No unsafe-code, PID-safety, event-log, or atomic-write regression found.

## Testing

Recorded `cargo-ci` and `docs-mechanical` gates passed. I did not rerun Cargo tests. `./scripts/jit-validate.sh` passes.

## Error handling and CLI contract

No regression found.

## Documentation

The new public heartbeat constant’s API documentation contradicts actual claim staleness behavior.

## JIT issue management

The sole dependency is done. Prior documentation links and naming findings were addressed, but the inaccurate generated scope remains.

1. **High** — [runtime-defaults.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/runtime-defaults.md:12) says only the “repository storage lock” reads `JIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` and all other file locks use the fixed default. However, [JsonFileStorage::new](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:123) passes the environment-derived timeout to its general `FileLocker`, which guards issue, index, gate, and event locks. This makes REQ-01’s required operational scope inaccurate.

2. **Medium** — [runtime_defaults.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/runtime_defaults.rs:15) says a heartbeat becomes stale after twice its interval, but indefinite claim leases are marked stale after the independent one-hour threshold in [claim_coordinator.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs:278). This newly introduced public API documentation is incorrect.

Total findings: 2
